# NDCG / MAP / MRR + Position Bias Drill -- Google R1 Prep

## Prerequisites

- Sorting + ranked list basics, graded vs binary relevance labels
- Probability and expectation (for examination hypothesis)
- LambdaMART / LTR context (see google_lambdarank_drill.md companion)

## Key Terms

- **DCG** (Discounted Cumulative Gain): Position-discounted sum of gains over the top-K ranked docs
- **NDCG** (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain): DCG divided by IDCG so scores are comparable across queries
- **IDCG** (Ideal DCG): DCG under the best possible ordering (sort by label desc)
- **MAP** (Mean Average Precision): Mean over queries of AP; AP averages precision at each relevant-hit rank
- **AP** (Average Precision): Sum of Precision@k times (k is a relevant hit), divided by # relevant docs
- **MRR** (Mean Reciprocal Rank): Mean of 1/rank of the first relevant doc; one-correct-answer tasks
- **IPW** (Inverse Propensity Weighting): Weight each click by 1 / P(examine | position) to debias training / eval
- **ULTR** (Unbiased Learning to Rank): Factor click = examine(pos) x relevance(q, d); serve the relevance tower only

## 1. **DCG** and **NDCG** -- Memorize This

Setup: for query q, rank K documents; each doc i at position p_i in 1..K has a graded label y_i in {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} (0 = irrelevant, 4 = perfect). Discount position using a log schedule that matches the empirical drop-off in user attention.

Numerator = gain, denominator = position discount:

$$\mathrm{DCG}@K \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{K}\;\frac{2^{y_i} - 1}{\log_2(i + 1)}$$

**IDCG** = DCG under the ideal ordering (sort labels desc):

$$\mathrm{IDCG}@K \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{K}\;\frac{2^{y^{\star}_{i}} - 1}{\log_2(i + 1)}$$

Normalize per query so NDCG across different queries is comparable:

$$\mathrm{NDCG}@K \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{DCG}@K}{\mathrm{IDCG}@K}\;\in\;[0,\,1]$$

Why the 2^y - 1 gain (exponential, not linear): exponential gain makes perfect documents (y=4) worth 15x a y=1 doc (2^4 - 1 = 15, 2^1 - 1 = 1), so label ties at the top cannot dominate; it also makes swap-delta algebra clean in LambdaRank -- only the exchanged positions' terms change.

Why log2(i + 1) discount (log, not linear): log discount is the classic web-click empirical fit -- CTR drops roughly like 1/log(rank) across measured search logs. Position 1 discount = 1/log2(2) = 1.0, position 10 is 1/log2(11) ~ 0.289, position 100 is ~0.150.

Oral shortcut: 'DCG = sum of (2^y - 1) / log2(i + 1). NDCG = DCG over IDCG so it is in [0, 1] and comparable across queries. Exponential gain rewards top-relevance docs, log discount matches user attention decay.'

## 2. **MAP** (Mean Average Precision) -- Binary-Label World

MAP assumes binary relevance y_i in {0, 1}. For a query with R relevant docs total, walk down the ranked list and record Precision@k at every rank k where a relevant doc shows up:

Per-query Average Precision:

$$\mathrm{AP} \;=\; \frac{1}{R}\,\sum_{k=1}^{N}\mathrm{Precision}@k \,\cdot\, \mathbb{1}[y_{(k)} = 1]$$

Running precision at rank k:

$$\mathrm{Precision}@k \;=\; \frac{|\{i\,:\,i\le k,\; y_{(i)} = 1\}|}{k}$$

MAP = mean **AP** over all queries:

$$\mathrm{MAP} \;=\; \frac{1}{|Q|}\,\sum_{q\in Q}\;\mathrm{AP}(q)$$

Why MAP is the wrong metric for graded relevance (Google panel trap):

- MAP thresholds labels to 0/1. Any y > 0 becomes a 'hit' -- a y=1 doc and a y=4 doc are indistinguishable. Swapping a perfect result with a marginally-relevant one costs zero MAP change.

- MAP has a position discount only implicitly (later hits get smaller Precision@k denominator), but it does not weight by label grade. Two rankings with identical relevant-positions but very different grade orderings score identically in MAP.

- MAP does not use a log discount -- it uses 1/rank via Precision@k. This is closer to **MRR**'s shape than to NDCG's and does not match observed user attention.

Rule of thumb: MAP for web-search evaluation with binary judgements (TREC-style old benchmarks), NDCG for graded labels (modern search / ranking), MRR for one-correct-answer QA / navigational queries.

Oral shortcut: 'MAP is binary-only; it cannot tell a perfect doc from a marginally-relevant one. For graded labels NDCG is the right metric because (2^y - 1) gain makes grade differences matter.'

## 3. MRR and the Metric Cheat Sheet

MRR assumes there is one correct answer per query (navigational search, single-answer QA). Reciprocal Rank = 1 / rank of that one correct doc; MRR averages across queries:

rank_q* = rank of the single correct doc for query q:

$$\mathrm{MRR} \;=\; \frac{1}{|Q|}\,\sum_{q\in Q}\;\frac{1}{\mathrm{rank}_q^{\star}}$$

MRR ignores everything after the first hit; it rewards 'getting one thing right early' rather than the overall shape of the list. Great for 'did Google send me to Wikipedia for 'Albert Einstein'' -- poor for 'rank the top 10 restaurants near me'.

**Ranking Metric Cheat Sheet**

| Metric | Label type | Position discount | Best for | Fails when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NDCG@K | Graded (0..4) | log2(i + 1) | Graded relevance ranking (web search, product, feed) | Only binary labels available; or ties dominate at top |
| MAP | Binary (0/1) | Implicit via Precision@k | Binary judgements, full-list precision-oriented eval | Graded relevance (cannot tell y=1 from y=4) |
| MRR | Binary (one correct) | 1/rank of first hit | Navigational search, single-answer QA, known-item | Multi-answer lists (ignores position 2..K entirely) |
| Precision@K | Binary (0/1) | None (hard cutoff) | Top-K screenshot quality at a fixed cutoff | Position sensitivity needed; graded grades matter |


## 4. Numerical Example -- MAP vs NDCG Disagree

Two ranked lists of 5 docs each for the same query. Graded labels are y in {0, 1, 2, 3}. MAP binarizes with threshold y > 0.

**List A** (graded labels in rank order): [3, 2, 1, 0, 0]

**List B** (graded labels in rank order): [1, 1, 3, 0, 0]

R = 3 relevant docs in both lists, K = 5. IDCG uses the ideal ordering [3, 2, 1, 0, 0], so IDCG is the same for both.

IDCG computation:

IDCG = 7 + 3/log2(3) + 1/log2(4):

$$\mathrm{IDCG} \;=\; \frac{2^{3}-1}{\log_2 2} + \frac{2^{2}-1}{\log_2 3} + \frac{2^{1}-1}{\log_2 4} \;=\; 7 + 1.893 + 0.500 \;\approx\; 9.393$$

DCG for List A (already ideal):

List A is the ideal ordering:

$$\mathrm{DCG}_A \;=\; \frac{7}{1.000} + \frac{3}{1.585} + \frac{1}{2.000} \;\approx\; 9.393 \;\Rightarrow\; \mathrm{NDCG}_A = 1.000$$

DCG for List B (best doc buried at rank 3):

y=3 doc sits at position 3, loses heavy discount:

$$\mathrm{DCG}_B \;=\; \frac{1}{1.000} + \frac{1}{1.585} + \frac{7}{2.000} \;\approx\; 1 + 0.631 + 3.500 \;=\; 5.131$$

NDCG penalty is severe -- 45 points lower than List A:

$$\mathrm{NDCG}_B \;=\; \frac{5.131}{9.393} \;\approx\; 0.546$$

MAP on the same lists (binarize: y > 0 -> relevant):

List A binarized = [1, 1, 1, 0, 0]; AP picks up every rank:

$$\mathrm{AP}_A \;=\; \tfrac{1}{3}\bigl(\tfrac{1}{1} + \tfrac{2}{2} + \tfrac{3}{3}\bigr) \;=\; 1.000$$

List B binarized = [1, 1, 1, 0, 0] -- same pattern, same AP:

$$\mathrm{AP}_B \;=\; \tfrac{1}{3}\bigl(\tfrac{1}{1} + \tfrac{2}{2} + \tfrac{3}{3}\bigr) \;=\; 1.000$$

Verdict: NDCG scores are 1.000 vs 0.546 (A wins decisively), MAP scores are 1.000 vs 1.000 (tie). Same docs, same binarized positions, but NDCG catches that the perfect doc was buried while MAP is blind to grade. This is exactly why Google / graded-label ranking teams ignore MAP.

Oral shortcut: 'Show the [3,2,1,0,0] vs [1,1,3,0,0] toy. MAP ties them at 1.0 because binarized positions are identical; NDCG separates them at 1.0 vs 0.55 because exponential gain punishes the buried y=3 doc.'

## 5. Position Bias Contaminates Offline NDCG

The trap: when labels come from click logs instead of human judgements, high-position docs get more clicks merely because users see them first. Offline NDCG computed on those click-labels rewards the ranker for reproducing the existing UI, not for actual relevance.

Examination hypothesis (Craswell et al. 2008 Cascade / PBM): a click requires two independent events -- the user has to look at position k AND judge the doc relevant.

Position bias = the examine factor; relevance is what we want to learn:

$$\Pr(\mathrm{click} \mid q, d, k) \;=\; \underbrace{\Pr(\mathrm{examine} \mid k)}_{\text{position-dependent}}\;\cdot\;\underbrace{\Pr(\mathrm{relevant} \mid q, d)}_{\text{what we want}}$$

Why this contaminates offline NDCG:

- Training labels = raw clicks. The model learns to reproduce P(click | q, d, k), which bakes in the position prior -- high ranks get positive labels simply for being shown at high ranks.

- Offline NDCG measured on those same logs looks great for any ranker that agrees with the current production ordering. NDCG deltas between a rival model and production are artificially small (positional agreement inflates the score).

- New-item / long-tail docs never appeared at high positions, so their click-labels are all zero -- not because they are irrelevant but because they were never examined. NDCG credits irrelevance it did not measure.

Fix #1 -- Inverse Propensity Weighting (**IPW**): estimate examination probability P(examine | k), then weight each training / eval example by 1 / P(examine | k) to remove position bias in expectation:

Down-weight top positions, up-weight buried ones:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{IPW}} \;=\; \sum_{(q, d, k)}\;\frac{1}{\Pr(\mathrm{examine} \mid k)}\;\cdot\;\ell\bigl(y_{q,d},\;\hat{y}_{q,d}\bigr)$$

- Estimate P(examine | k) via result-swap randomization (rare in prod) or EM on regression clicks. High variance at low examine probabilities -- standard fix is to clip 1/P(examine) at a ceiling (e.g. 10 or 20).

Fix #2 -- Unbiased LTR / PAL (Position-Aware Learning): factor the click model into a relevance tower and a position tower; train jointly, serve only the relevance tower:

Two-tower click model; drop the position tower at inference:

$$\Pr(\mathrm{click} \mid q, d, k) \;=\; \sigma\bigl(f_{\mathrm{rel}}(q, d)\bigr)\;\cdot\;\sigma\bigl(f_{\mathrm{pos}}(k)\bigr)$$

- Production choice at DoorDash / Google / Etsy: PAL with a learned position feature that is zeroed at serve time. Cheaper than IPW (no propensity estimation), and variance is bounded.

Offline-NDCG guardrail even with fixes: always pair offline NDCG with a second metric that is less biased -- either human-judged NDCG on a sampled slate, or a counterfactual IPS estimator on uniformly-randomized serving traffic -- before shipping.

Oral shortcut: 'Offline NDCG on click-labels is contaminated by the examine factor. Fixes are IPW (weight by 1 / P(examine | k)) or **ULTR** (two-tower click = relevance x position, serve relevance only). Always validate with human-judged or counterfactual NDCG before trusting the offline delta.'

### 2-Minute Oral Self-Check

- [ ] Write DCG@K = sum (2^y_i - 1) / log2(i + 1) from memory
- [ ] Write NDCG@K = DCG / IDCG and state range [0, 1]
- [ ] Explain 2^y - 1 (exponential gain) and log2(i+1) (attention decay)
- [ ] State MAP formula: AP = (1/R) sum Precision@k * 1[y_k relevant]
- [ ] Name why MAP fails graded labels (binarize collapses y=1 and y=4)
- [ ] Walk the [3,2,1,0,0] vs [1,1,3,0,0] toy: NDCG 1.0 vs 0.55, MAP 1.0 vs 1.0
- [ ] Write click = P(examine | k) * P(relevant | q, d) (examination hypothesis)
- [ ] Explain why offline NDCG on click-logs is inflated for production ranker
- [ ] IPW fix: weight by 1 / P(examine | k); note high variance + clipping
- [ ] ULTR / PAL fix: two-tower click = relevance * position, serve relevance only
- [ ] Guardrail: pair offline NDCG with human-judged slate or counterfactual IPS
